Teacher-screen names, classes and figures are made up.

lesson.title: Cell division and transport
lesson.body: Cells in your body divide to grow, repair damaged tissue and replace worn-out cells. This follows the cell cycle. Most of it is spent in interphase, when the cell copies its DNA, before mitosis makes two identical cells.

flash.typed: moving things from low to high concentration using energy
flash.model: Moving substances from a lower to a higher concentration, using energy from respiration.

practice.question: A 12 V battery is connected to a 6 Ω resistor. Calculate the current flowing through the resistor.
working: V = I × R, so I = V ÷ R

practice.question: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
practice.feedback: Right. Aerobic respiration happens in the mitochondria.

exam.question: Explain why gamma rays are more dangerous to human cells than radio waves.
exam.answer: Gamma rays have a much higher frequency than radio waves, so they carry more energy. This energy can ionise atoms and damage the DNA in cells, which can cause mutations or cancer.
exam.well: Frequency, energy and the damage, linked in order.

q1.question: Which process needs energy from respiration?
why: Not quite. Diffusion needs no energy:
particles move down a concentration gradient.
Active transport moves them up it, using energy.

q2.question: What happens to the resistance of a thermistor as the temperature increases?
